The international data can help us evaluate a theory of growth, such as the Solow model, because they show us whether the theory’s predictions are borne out in the world. But often more than one theory can explain the same facts. n Alternative Perspectives on Population Growth The Solow growth model highlights the interaction between population growth and capital accumulation. In this model, high population growth reduces output per worker because rapid growth in the number of workers forces the capital stock to be spread more thinly, so in the steady state, each worker is equipped with less capital. The model omits some other potential effects of population growth. Here we consider two—one emphasizing the interaction of population with natural resources, the other emphasizing the interaction of population with technology.
